docs.text: Driver WS2812_RMT Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for single-wire addressable RGB and RGBW LEDs (WS2812, SK6812 and compatible), sent as a timed bit stream through a small port class. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The core is platform-free: it keeps the pixels, encodes the byte stream and works out the waveform from the datasheet windows and the tick rate your port really runs at. The port sends the bytes. On ESP32 that is the RMT transmitter, and the repository ships that port as an example. MCU-bound through the port The driver needs a peripheral that can send a timed bit stream ( bus: pio in driver.yml ). On ESP32 that is the RMT transmitter. On another MCU you write a port over its own peripheral: Porting . Addressable LED WS2812B Worldsemi (and the SK6812 family of Opsco) Interface One data line, 800 kbit/s: the length of each high pulse is the bit, 24 bits per pixel (32 on SK6812RGBW) Supply 3.7 V to 5.3 V (WS2812B V5, absolute maximum); see Hardware for each part Timing Four windows, each from the datasheet, and a reset above 280 µs (V5): see Timing What you get ¶ One object per strip , with a fixed capacity and no heap. No I/O until EnsureInitialized() . See API guide . The right waveform for your part. A named variant per datasheet generation, or your own windows with Custom . A waveform outside the windows cannot reach the wire. See Timing . Errors you can act on : Result<T> with an Error . See Contract . Colour order, brightness and gamma as data, not code. See Colour . Tested without hardware against a model written from the datasheets. See Testing and CI . docs.text: API guide ¶ The driver by task. Every fallible call returns Result<T> : check it with ok() or if (result) , then use value or error . Nothing throws, and nothing is allocated. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Worldsemi WS2812B-V5 V5.0: 24 bit data, GRB, high bit first: Composition of 24bit Data, p. 4 Cascade and data transmission method: Data Transmission Method, p. 4 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Task Calls Start EnsureInitialized() , IsInitialized() Colours SetPixel() , GetPixel() , Fill() , Clear() , SetBrightness() , SetGamma() Send Show() Supply PowerOn() , PowerOff() Raw access TraceWire() , GetLastWire() Inspect Length() , ChannelsPerPixel() , CurrentWaveform() , FrameTimeUs() , GetConfig() Pure functions ResolveWaveform() , WaveformInWindow() , EncodeFrame() , DecodeWire() , Wheel() , ExtractWhite() , ... The object ¶ ws2812_rmt :: Ws2812Rmt < MyPort , 60 > strip ( port , config ); The second template argument is the capacity: the object holds 60 colours and the byte buffer for them (4 bytes per pixel at most), so no heap is needed and the buffers live where you put the object. Config::pixel_count can be smaller than the capacity (0 means the whole capacity). The constructor does no I/O and cannot fail. Start ¶ EnsureInitialized() checks the configuration, asks the port to open its channel, asks for the tick rate and resolves the waveform. It returns InvalidArgument (the configuration is invalid, no port call made), Bus (the port failed) or TimingUnreachable (the rate cannot meet a window). After a failure the driver is still uninitialised and the next call starts again. After a success it returns Ok at once. Set and show ¶ SetPixel() stores a logical colour and returns InvalidArgument for an index past the strip (nothing changes). Fill() , Clear() , SetBrightness() and SetGamma() never fail and do no I/O. Show() encodes every pixel (gamma, then brightness, in the wire order) and asks the port to send it; it blocks until the frame and the reset are out. A failed Show() leaves the pixels intact: call it again. Brightness and colour order ¶ Colour has both, and Configuration every field of Config . api_tasks.cpp // An SK6812RGBW strip: four channels, white last. Rev 01 and Rev 03 datasheets send red first. ws2812_rmt :: Config RgbwConfig ( bool old_revision ) { ws2812_rmt :: Config c = ws2812_rmt :: Config :: Default (); c . variant = ws2812_rmt :: Variant :: Sk6812Rgbw ; if ( old_revision ) { c . use_default_order = false ; c . order = ws2812_rmt :: kOrderRgbw ; // red and green swapped on the strip means: use this } return c ; } Raw access ¶ TraceWire(bytes) sends bytes exactly as given, as one frame with the resolved waveform: no order, brightness or gamma, no retry, the stored pixels untouched. It finds the order of an unknown strip (send {0xFF, 0, 0} and see which colour lights). GetLastWire() returns the bytes Show() encoded last, with no I/O, valid until the next Show() ; compare it with what a logic analyser captured. Supply ¶ PowerOn() drives the port's power pin active and waits Config::power_on_settle_us ; PowerOff() drives it inactive and keeps the waveform. A port without a GpioSet() hook gets Unsupported . A port with the hook starts unpowered: call PowerOn() before the first Show() . A port with the hook but no pin must return true from GpioSet() . After PowerOff() , Show() and TraceWire() return NotPowered and send nothing, because a driven DIN on an unpowered strip back-feeds it ( Hardware ). api_tasks.cpp // The strip supply on a switch: the port implements GpioSet(), the driver sequences it. ws2812_rmt :: Error ShowAfterPowerUp ( Strip & strip ) { if ( auto r = strip . PowerOn (); ! r ) { return r . error ; // Unsupported (no GpioSet hook), NotInitialized or Bus } return strip . Show (). error ; } Errors ¶ api_tasks.cpp const char * Describe ( ws2812_rmt :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case ws2812_rmt :: Error :: TimingUnreachable : return "the port's tick rate cannot place a window: use 20 MHz or more" ; case ws2812_rmt :: Error :: Bus : return "the port failed: channel, rate, send, timeout or underrun" ; default : return ws2812_rmt :: ToString ( e ); } } The pixels are write-only: no identity, no status, no checksum. So Timeout , DeviceIdMismatch , Crc , Busy and DeviceFault are never returned; a timeout or an underrun that the port detects arrives as Bus . See Contract for each error.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: the core, the port contract, and your port. The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/ws2812_rmt.hpp public calls ; inc/ws2812_rmt_gpio_interface.hpp GpioInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layer Files Owns Core inc/ws2812_rmt.hpp , src/ws2812_rmt.ipp Lifecycle, the pixel and wire buffers, Show() , power Pure functions inc/ws2812_rmt_functions.hpp , inc/ws2812_rmt_gamma.hpp Waveform resolution, encoding, frame time, Validate() , the gamma table Types inc/ws2812_rmt_types.hpp Error , Result<T> , Colour , Timing , the profile table, Waveform , Config Port contract inc/ws2812_rmt_gpio_interface.hpp The CRTP base, CtrlPin , GpioSignal , the Ws2812RmtPort concept Platform port Your class The channel, the tick rate, the stream, optionally the supply pin The part has no read-back, so there is no register map and no frame to parse: the core writes a byte stream and decides what waveform it is sent with. The functions are free constexpr functions with no state, so the tests check each against an independent oracle and a fixed configuration can be proved at build time. One call, in order ¶ SetPixel() and friends store logical colours. No I/O. Show() walks the pixels once, applies gamma then brightness, writes the bytes in the configured order into the object's wire buffer, and gives the port the span, the resolved waveform and a timeout. The port sends the stream and the reset, and returns true or false . The waveform is resolved once, at EnsureInitialized() , from the windows and the tick rate. It is not recomputed per frame, and it is not changed by anything the caller can set after that. Why a capacity template argument ¶ The driver owns its buffers (no heap, no caller-owned span that could dangle, handbook KB-CPP20-044), so the capacity is a template argument. A smaller Config::pixel_count uses part of it. One object serves one strip. Next: Contract .

docs.text: Changelog ¶ What changed in each release of the driver. Entries under Breaking need source changes in code that used the affected API. [Unreleased] ¶ Added ¶ WS2812_RMT driver, first version: the pixel and wire buffers of a strip with a fixed capacity, the byte encoder (colour order, brightness, optional gamma 2.2), and a waveform resolver that converts the datasheet windows of the chosen variant to ticks at the port's real rate and refuses a rate that cannot meet them. Variants Ws2812 , Ws2812bPreV5 , Ws2812bV5 (default), Ws2812c , Ws2812d , Sk6812 , Sk6812Rgbw , Sk6812Mini and Custom , each the intersection of the windows of the datasheets it covers (see docs/datasheets.yml ). Port contract with four required hooks ( EnsureInitialized() , ResolutionHz() , Transmit() , DelayUs() ) and optional GpioSet() and Log() ; PowerOn() and PowerOff() for a switched strip supply. Raw access: TraceWire() sends bytes as given, GetLastWire() shows the bytes of the last Show() . Pure functions: ResolveWaveform() , WaveformInWindow() , EncodeFrame() , DecodeWire() , FrameTimeNs() , MaxRefreshHz() , MaxPixelsAtRate() , MinLogicHighMv() , Wheel() , ExtractWhite() , Validate() . Host example with a simulated strip, ESP32 RMT port and two ESP-IDF examples, Kconfig menu, and a documentation site with the datasheet map, timing and colour pages. Host tests against a model of the pixels written from the datasheets, and a fuzz target with the driver's promises. Changed ¶ Review fixes made before the first release. A failed Transmit() now makes the driver wait one full reset ( DelayUs , line low) before the next Show() or TraceWire() , so a frame cut half-way is never continued. DelayUs() is a required port hook. Show() and TraceWire() return the new Error::NotPowered (17) after PowerOff() , even when the pin write failed. The longest low inside a frame is derived from the smallest latch time of the documents of a variant ( PreV5 50 us, Sk6812 50 us, 20 us for the later SK6812 sheets), with a 10 percent margin, instead of one 50 us figure. MinLogicHighMv(Ws2812bV5, ...) returns the strictest of the revisions (0.63 x VDD, at least 2.7 V): 3150 mV at 5 V. Named variants are refused below kMinResolutionHz (now 20 MHz) with TimingUnreachable ; Custom is exempt. The V5 profile aims T1H and T1L at 650 ns (T0H 350 ns) for margin. A port with a GpioSet() hook starts unpowered: Show() and TraceWire() return NotPowered until PowerOn() succeeds (also after a failed PowerOn() ); a port with the hook but no pin returns true from it. ResolveWaveform() returns TimingUnreachable when a low phase would exceed the max_gap_ticks it hands the port. New pure function ResolveRmtRate() (the real tick rate of the ESP32 RMT: the divider rounded to the nearest integer and the group prescaler search of ESP-IDF v5.5, with a ppm tolerance), used by the ESP32 port and tested on the host. The ESP32 port also derives mem_block_symbols per target (multiple of the memory block) and sets the RMT interrupt priority. Removed the unused _u32 literal and LiteralOutOfRange . Datasheet map: the Watterott copy is revision V6.1 (2022-09), the Hestore copy V6.0 (2021-12) and the 1313 package sheet are listed; input level text in README, troubleshooting and the DIN pin row follows the per-revision values; both reference circuits show the 74HCT buffer and the 330 ohm series resistor. The ESP32 port reports the tick rate it really got and refuses a clock more than 1000 ppm off the profile; it documents that it cannot see underruns. Documentation: input levels per datasheet revision, a corrected reference circuit (load switch, 74HCT buffer, series resistor), relabelled datasheet entries (Watterott V6.1; the Hestore copy is V6.0, 2021), "mirror" instead of "vendor page" in the generated tables. Both ESP32 examples call PowerOn() in their start-up (the custom example never did, so every Show() returned NotPowered ); the start-up of each example is a Start() function that the host tests run against stand-ins of the ESP-IDF headers ( tests/esp32_stub/ ). The basic example checks every SetPixel() result. The ESP32 port requests 32 MHz on the ESP32-H2 (its RMT runs from the 32 MHz crystal, where 20 MHz is not reachable) and adds two RTOS ticks to the frame wait, which ESP-IDF rounds down to whole ticks. The ESP32 port reads back the rate its channel really got ( rmt_get_channel_resolution() ) and refuses to start when it differs from the computed one, as when another channel fixed the shared group prescaler first. The profile table passes U literals through explicitly qualified calls, and the conditional and std::min results widened to uint64_t are cast explicitly. Not verified Hardware: the ESP32 port and the driver have not been run on a strip.

docs.text: Review fixes made before the first release. A failed Transmit() now makes the driver wait one full reset ( DelayUs , line low) before the next Show() or TraceWire() , so a frame cut half-way is never continued. DelayUs() is a required port hook. Show() and TraceWire() return the new Error::NotPowered (17) after PowerOff() , even when the pin write failed. The longest low inside a frame is derived from the smallest latch time of the documents of a variant ( PreV5 50 us, Sk6812 50 us, 20 us for the later SK6812 sheets), with a 10 percent margin, instead of one 50 us figure. MinLogicHighMv(Ws2812bV5, ...) returns the strictest of the revisions (0.63 x VDD, at least 2.7 V): 3150 mV at 5 V. Named variants are refused below kMinResolutionHz (now 20 MHz) with TimingUnreachable ; Custom is exempt. The V5 profile aims T1H and T1L at 650 ns (T0H 350 ns) for margin. A port with a GpioSet() hook starts unpowered: Show() and TraceWire() return NotPowered until PowerOn() succeeds (also after a failed PowerOn() ); a port with the hook but no pin returns true from it. ResolveWaveform() returns TimingUnreachable when a low phase would exceed the max_gap_ticks it hands the port. New pure function ResolveRmtRate() (the real tick rate of the ESP32 RMT: the divider rounded to the nearest integer and the group prescaler search of ESP-IDF v5.5, with a ppm tolerance), used by the ESP32 port and tested on the host. The ESP32 port also derives mem_block_symbols per target (multiple of the memory block) and sets the RMT interrupt priority. Removed the unused _u32 literal and LiteralOutOfRange . Datasheet map: the Watterott copy is revision V6.1 (2022-09), the Hestore copy V6.0 (2021-12) and the 1313 package sheet are listed; input level text in README, troubleshooting and the DIN pin row follows the per-revision values; both reference circuits show the 74HCT buffer and the 330 ohm series resistor. The ESP32 port reports the tick rate it really got and refuses a clock more than 1000 ppm off the profile; it documents that it cannot see underruns. Documentation: input levels per datasheet revision, a corrected reference circuit (load switch, 74HCT buffer, series resistor), relabelled datasheet entries (Watterott V6.1; the Hestore copy is V6.0, 2021), "mirror" instead of "vendor page" in the generated tables. Both ESP32 examples call PowerOn() in their start-up (the custom example never did, so every Show() returned NotPowered ); the start-up of each example is a Start() function that the host tests run against stand-ins of the ESP-IDF headers ( tests/esp32_stub/ ). The basic example checks every SetPixel() result. The ESP32 port requests 32 MHz on the ESP32-H2 (its RMT runs from the 32 MHz crystal, where 20 MHz is not reachable) and adds two RTOS ticks to the frame wait, which ESP-IDF rounds down to whole ticks. The ESP32 port reads back the rate its channel really got ( rmt_get_channel_resolution() ) and refuses to start when it differs from the computed one, as when another channel fixed the shared group prescaler first. The profile table passes U literals through explicitly qualified calls, and the conditional and std::min results widened to uint64_t are cast explicitly. Not verified Hardware: the ESP32 port and the driver have not been run on a strip.

docs.text: Colour ¶ The colour order, RGBW, brightness and gamma: what goes on the wire for a colour you set. Datasheet sections this page relies on 24 bit data, GRB, high bit first: Worldsemi WS2812B-V5 V5.0, Composition of 24bit Data, p. 4 32 bit data and its order: RGBW (revisions 01 and 03): Opsco SK6812RGBX-XX Rev. 03, 13. The data structure of 32bit, p. 6 32 bit data and its order: GRBW: Opsco SK6812RGBX-XX Rev. 07, 13. The data structure of 32bit, p. 9 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . What a pixel receives ¶ A pixel takes 24 bits (32 on SK6812RGBW), high bit first, one byte per colour channel, and the order of the channels is fixed by the part. Pixel 0 is the one nearest the controller; a frame is every pixel back to back, then the reset. Parts Order on the wire Datasheet WS2812, WS2812B, WS2812C, WS2812D, SK6812, SK6812MINI G, R, B ( kOrderGrb ) V5, p. 4 SK6812RGBW Rev 07 G, R, B, W ( kOrderGrbw ) skw-07, p. 9 SK6812RGBW Rev 01 and Rev 03 R, G, B, W ( kOrderRgbw ) skw-03, p. 6 The three SK6812RGBW documents disagree. Variant::Sk6812Rgbw defaults to GRBW, the later revision. If red and green are swapped on your strip, it is an older part: set the order to RGBW. api_tasks.cpp // An SK6812RGBW strip: four channels, white last. Rev 01 and Rev 03 datasheets send red first. ws2812_rmt :: Config RgbwConfig ( bool old_revision ) { ws2812_rmt :: Config c = ws2812_rmt :: Config :: Default (); c . variant = ws2812_rmt :: Variant :: Sk6812Rgbw ; if ( old_revision ) { c . use_default_order = false ; c . order = ws2812_rmt :: kOrderRgbw ; // red and green swapped on the strip means: use this } return c ; } The order is data: a ColourOrder of up to four channels. Any permutation of R, G, B and (for four channels) W is valid, which covers clone parts that use another order. Validate() refuses an order with a repeated channel, a white channel in a three-channel order, or a count other than 3 or 4. colour.cpp // The pure encoder, without a strip: what the wire carries for one pixel. bool EncodeOne () { std :: array < uint8_t , 3 > wire {}; const ws2812_rmt :: Colour c { 0x12 , 0x34 , 0x56 , 0 }; const size_t n = ws2812_rmt :: EncodePixel ( c , ws2812_rmt :: kOrderGrb , 255 , ws2812_rmt :: Gamma :: None , wire ); return ( n == 3U ) && ( wire [ 0 ] == 0x34U ) && ( wire [ 1 ] == 0x12U ) && ( wire [ 2 ] == 0x56U ); // green first } Brightness and gamma ¶ Config::brightness and SetBrightness() scale every channel linearly at Show() : 255 leaves a value unchanged, 0 is off, and the value is rounded, not truncated. The stored colours are never changed, so brightness is reversible. Gamma, off by default, maps each value through a 2.2 table before brightness: api_tasks.cpp using Strip = ws2812_rmt :: Ws2812Rmt < MyPort , 30 > ; void Dim ( Strip & strip , bool night ) { strip . SetBrightness ( night ? 20 : 255 ); // linear; the stored colours are untouched strip . SetGamma ( ws2812_rmt :: Gamma :: Gamma22 ); } The pixels have 256 PWM levels per channel and nothing else: brightness and gamma are convenience of the driver, not chip features. A strip dimmed by brightness 20 has about 5 levels per channel left; if you need smooth fades at low light, dim with the strip's supply or work in a wider colour type of your own. White ¶ An RGBW pixel has a white die. ExtractWhite() moves the common part of red, green and blue into white, for a strip that should show an RGB colour with the white die. It is never applied implicitly: colour.cpp // RGB colour on an RGBW strip with the white die: the common part of R, G and B moves to W. ws2812_rmt :: Colour Warm () { return ws2812_rmt :: ExtractWhite ( ws2812_rmt :: Colour { 200 , 100 , 50 , 0 }); // {150, 50, 0, 50} } Wheel ¶ Wheel() returns a fully saturated colour for a position from 0 to 255 (red to green to blue to red). It is a helper for demos; the driver has no animations or effects: colour.cpp // An animation is ordinary code: the driver has Wheel() and SetPixel(), not effects. template < typename Strip > void Rainbow ( Strip & strip , uint8_t phase ) { for ( size_t i = 0 ; i < strip . Length (); ++ i ) { const auto position = static_cast < uint8_t > ( phase + (( i * 256U ) / strip . Length ())); static_cast < void > ( strip . SetPixel ( i , ws2812_rmt :: Wheel ( position ))); } }

Config::Default() suits a current WS2812B. The constructor stores the configuration; EnsureInitialized() checks it before any port call. Validate(config, capacity) is constexpr , so a fixed configuration can be proved at build time (see the static_assert in the Custom example below). Field Default Meaning variant Ws2812bV5 The timing generation: Timing use_default_order true false uses order ; always false for Custom order empty The wire order of the channels: Colour brightness 255 Linear dimming at start, 0 to 255 gamma None The transfer curve at start pixel_count 0 Pixels in the strip; 0 means the whole capacity reset_us 0 Reset low time; 0 means the datasheet minimum plus 20 µs. A value must exceed the minimum power_on_settle_us 1000 Wait after PowerOn() ; no datasheet value (an assumption) transmit_slack_ms 20 Added to the frame time to form the timeout the port is given custom all zero The timing of Variant::Custom ; must stay zero for a named variant What Validate refuses ¶ An unknown variant or gamma; a custom timing on a named variant; an inconsistent custom timing on Custom ; an invalid order, one with a channel count that differs from the variant's, or a missing order on Custom ; a reset_us that is not above the minimum or above 10 ms; a pixel_count above the capacity; a capacity of 0 or above 65 536 pixels; a settle above 1 s or a slack above 60 s. It returns InvalidArgument and the port is not touched. Kconfig (ESP-IDF) ¶ idf.py menuconfig has a "WS2812_RMT addressable LED driver" menu: the variant, the start brightness, the reset time (0 for the datasheet minimum plus 20 µs) and the power-on settle time. The values reach the code only through ws2812_rmt_kconfig.hpp ; outside ESP-IDF KconfigDefaults() equals Config::Default() . The strip's pin, length and tick rate belong to the application and its port, not to the driver. configuration.cpp ws2812_rmt :: Error StartFromMenuconfig ( MyPort & port ) { static ws2812_rmt :: Ws2812Rmt < MyPort , 60 > strip ( port , ws2812_rmt :: KconfigDefaults ()); return strip . EnsureInitialized (). error ; } A part with its own timing ¶ Variant::Custom takes the windows from Config::custom and nothing from the named parts. Each Range is a minimum, a maximum (0 for none) and the nominal value the driver aims for. A Custom part states its order and its reset: configuration.cpp // A part whose datasheet is not among the named variants: state its timing and its order yourself. constexpr ws2812_rmt :: Config MyLedConfig () { ws2812_rmt :: Config c = ws2812_rmt :: Config :: Default (); c . variant = ws2812_rmt :: Variant :: Custom ; c . custom . t0h = { 250 , 450 , 350 }; // min, max, nominal in nanoseconds c . custom . t0l = { 700 , 1200 , 900 }; c . custom . t1h = { 700 , 1100 , 850 }; c . custom . t1l = { 300 , 700 , 450 }; c . custom . reset_min_ns = 60'000 ; // the low time that must be exceeded to latch c . use_default_order = false ; // a Custom part always states its order c . order = ws2812_rmt :: kOrderGrb ; return c ; } static_assert ( ws2812_rmt :: Validate ( MyLedConfig (), 30 ). ok ()); // proved at build time Copy the numbers from your part's datasheet with the section and page in a comment. docs.text: Contract ¶ What the WS2812_RMT driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. The pixels start black. EnsureInitialized() is the only start-up call. It checks the configuration ( InvalidArgument , no port call), lets the port open its channel and report its tick rate ( Bus ), and resolves the waveform ( TimingUnreachable ). After it has succeeded it returns Ok with no I/O; after a failure the driver stays uninitialised. Show() , PowerOn() , PowerOff() , CurrentWaveform() and FrameTimeUs() return NotInitialized before it has succeeded, and Show() makes no port call then. The waveform lies inside the windows. Every waveform the driver gives the port is inside the declared windows (every document of a named variant, or the declared window of Custom ), with the reset above the minimum, at the tick rate the port reported. A rate that cannot do that is refused, whatever the rate (including 0 and 2^32 - 1). Nothing is sent after InvalidArgument or TimingUnreachable , and nothing before a successful start. The wire has exactly Length() x ChannelsPerPixel() bytes, in the order of the configuration, after gamma and brightness. A failed Transmit() leaves the pixels intact and the driver usable. The next Show() or TraceWire() first waits one full reset ( port.DelayUs , line low), so a frame cut half-way is never continued by the next one, then sends the same frame. A port with a GpioSet() hook starts unpowered, and after PowerOff() (even when the pin write failed) Show() and TraceWire() return NotPowered and send nothing until PowerOn() succeeds. The reason: an input above VDD + 0.7 V is outside the absolute maximum ratings (WS2812B-V5 V5.0, p. 2), so DIN is not driven while the supply may be off. After a failed PowerOff() the LEDs may keep their last colours; recover with PowerOff() again, or with PowerOn() , Clear() , Show() , PowerOff() ( Limitations ). Every port failure (open, rate, send, timeout, power pin) propagates as Bus . An underrun is reported only if the port detects it; the ESP32 example cannot see one, so a starved frame is not reported (see Limitations). Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates ws2812_rmt_version.h Your port A timed bit stream, its real tick rate, optionally a supply pin Threading ¶ Not thread-safe; takes no lock. One owner task, or one mutex around every call. Do not call it from an ISR: Show() blocks until the frame is out. Errors ¶ Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 Before EnsureInitialized() succeeded InvalidArgument 2 Validate() failed, or a pixel index is out of range Bus 3 A port hook returned false Unsupported 9 PowerOn() or PowerOff() on a port without GpioSet() TimingUnreachable 16 The port's tick rate cannot meet a window, or a low phase would exceed the gap limit NotPowered 17 Show() or TraceWire() before PowerOn() succeeded (port with GpioSet() ) or after PowerOff() Timeout , DeviceIdMismatch , Crc , Busy and DeviceFault are never returned: the pixels have no read-back path, so there is no identity, no status and no checksum to fail, and a port reports a timeout as false . Memory ¶ No heap, exceptions, RTTI or static mutable state. The object holds a port reference, the Config , the colours ( capacity x 4 bytes) and the wire bytes ( capacity x 4 bytes). Platform ¶ Platform-free; the ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example. The driver reaches the peripheral only through the port. Deviations from the standard ¶ None.

docs.text: Examples ¶ One folder per platform under examples/ , each with its own port, built by CI on every pull request. The driver itself has no platform code; Platforms lists what exists. Host ¶ examples/host/ runs the driver on any PC against a simulated strip, through the host port host_ws2812_rmt_port.hpp . No hardware: cmake -S examples/host -B build-example && cmake --build build-example && ./build-example/ws2812_rmt_host_example It shows one pixel, a rainbow and an RGBW frame, and reads back what the simulated chain of pixels latched. The host tests build it with warnings as errors and run it (CTest ws2812_rmt_host_example ). ESP32 ¶ ESP-IDF applications that run the driver on an ESP32 with the RMT transmitter; the wiring is in the example folder's README and the port in esp32_ws2812_rmt_port.hpp . The project points EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at the repository root, which is the driver's ESP-IDF component. docs.text: Hardware ¶ The strip's pins, input levels, supply and wiring, as the driver uses them. The chip is a family of parts with the same four signals; the pin order and the levels differ per part. Datasheet sections this page relies on Pins and package: six pin 5050: Worldsemi WS2812 undated, PIN configuration, p. 2 Typical application circuit: Worldsemi WS2812B undated, Typical application circuit, p. 5 Input levels VIH and VIL: Worldsemi WS2812B-V5 V5.0, Electrical Characteristics, p. 2 Supply range and logical input voltage: Worldsemi WS2812B-V5 V5.0, Absolute Maximum Ratings, p. 2 Pins and package: four pin 5050: Worldsemi WS2812B-V5 V5.0, PIN Configuration, p. 2 Propagation delay DIN to DOUT: Worldsemi WS2812B-V5 V5.0, Switching Characteristics, p. 3 Input level 0.63 x VDD (later V5 family sheets): Worldsemi WS2812B-V5 V6.1, Electrical Characteristics, p. 3 Input levels of the SK6812: Opsco SK6812RGBW Rev. 01, Electrical Characteristics, p. 4 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Pins ¶ Every part has DIN (data from the controller), DOUT (data to the next pixel), VDD and VSS. The six-pin parts add a separate control supply. The pin numbers differ between parts, so check the drawing of your part's datasheet: Package Parts Pins Datasheet 5050, 4 pin, 5.0 x 5.4 x 1.57 mm WS2812B, WS2812C, WS2812B V5 and V6 1 VDD, 2 DOUT, 3 VSS, 4 DIN V5, p. 2 5050, 6 pin WS2812, WS2812S 1 DOUT, 2 DIN, 3 VCC (control supply), 4 NC, 5 VDD (LED supply), 6 VSS WS2812, p. 2 2020, 4 pin WS2812B-2020, WS2812C-2020, WS2812-2020 1 DO, 2 GND, 3 DI, 4 VDD WS2812B-2020, p. 2 MINI, 4 pin SK6812MINI, SK6812MINI-E 1 VDD, 2 DOUT, 3 GND, 4 DIN SK6812MINI-E, p. 4 8 mm round, through-hole WS2812D-F8 1 DOUT, 2 VDD, 3 GND, 4 DIN WS2812D-F8, p. 2 5050 (SK6812) SK6812, SK6812RGBW the Rev 01 sheet and the later revisions list different orders see below The SK6812 Rev 01 sheet disagrees with its own later revisions on the pin order of the 5050 package. Trust the silkscreen or the drawing of the sheet that matches your strip, and where they differ test one pixel before wiring a strip. The driver does not depend on the pin order: DIN is whatever pin your port drives. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( ws2812_rmt_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ws2812-rmt.git external/driver-ws2812-rmt git submodule update --init external/driver-ws2812-rmt Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-ws2812-rmt ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE ws2812_rmt::ws2812_rmt ) ws2812_rmt::ws2812_rmt is an alias of the ws2812_rmt INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect WS2812_RMT_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver WS2812_RMT_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-ws2812-rmt -B build-ws2812_rmt cmake --install build-ws2812_rmt --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( ws2812_rmt 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE ws2812_rmt::ws2812_rmt ) The target is ws2812_rmt::ws2812_rmt in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated ws2812_rmt_version.h go to include/ws2812_rmt/inc/ , the template implementation to include/ws2812_rmt/src/ws2812_rmt.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-ws2812-rmt) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-ws2812-rmt (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ws2812-rmt.git components/ws2812_rmt ws2812_rmt (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml ws2812_rmt (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : ws2812_rmt : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ws2812-rmt.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES ws2812_rmt (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. docs.text: Limitations ¶ What the driver does not cover, what it assumes where the datasheets are silent, and what is not verified. Each assumption has a knob, and the knob is named. Not covered ¶ WS2812E is not named. No datasheet for it could be obtained, so the driver does not guess its timing. Hold its sheet and use Custom , or ask for a named variant. WS2812D-F5 (same family as the F8, unverified) and the vendor's current WS2812B V7 sheet were not obtained. WS2811 and other external driver ICs with a 400 kbit/s mode, dual-signal parts with a backup data line, SPI-clocked pixels with a separate clock line, and 16-bit-per-channel parts: different frame or wire. The original WS2812's low-speed mode (400 kbit/s minimum, no windows given): reachable through Custom . Animations, effects and colour-space conversions: the driver sends colours. Wheel() and ExtractWhite() are helpers, not an effects engine. Underruns are not detected by the reference ESP32 port: the RMT TX driver reports no underrun, so a starved frame latches early and shows stale pixels without an error. Error::Bus for an underrun appears only for a port that can see one. Prevent it with DMA, a larger channel memory, and the bench step in Porting . Sk6812Mini has three colour channels (the MINI and MINI-E sheets); a four-channel mini LED is a different part: use Sk6812Rgbw , or Custom windows with its datasheet. The SK6812MINIRGBX sheet ( skm in the Datasheet map) describes such an RGBW part (CSPM1411RGBW-IC-6): Sk6812Mini takes only its timing windows, and the Sk6812Rgbw waveform also meets them. A failed PowerOff() (the pin write failed) leaves the supply in doubt, and the driver then refuses every frame, a blank one included, with NotPowered : DIN must not be driven while VDD may be off (input at most VDD + 0.7 V, WS2812B-V5 V5.0, Absolute Maximum Ratings, p. 2). The LEDs may keep their last colours. To recover, call PowerOff() again, or, when the supply is on after all, PowerOn() , Clear() , Show() and PowerOff() . A port with a GpioSet() hook starts unpowered: Show() and TraceWire() return NotPowered until PowerOn() succeeds. A port with the hook but no pin ( pins.power < 0 in the ESP32 example) returns true from it, because the supply is always on. PowerOn() and PowerOff() return Unsupported when the port has no hook. The ESP32 port shares the RMT group clock with every other RMT channel on the C3, C5, C6, H2, S3 and P4. A channel created earlier at another rate can leave this one at a rate the waveform does not fit; the port reads the real rate back after creating its channel and refuses to start ( Bus ) on a mismatch, so it never sends wrong colours, but it cannot share the group with such a channel. It reads the rate through rmt_get_channel_resolution() , an internal ESP-IDF function ( esp_private/rmt.h , present in v5.5) that a later ESP-IDF may change. Mixed generations in one chain: there may be no waveform legal for both ( Timing ). docs.text: Mechanization policy ¶ Where each defect class of the catalogue is caught, and how a class moves to a cheaper catch. The goal: a defect is found by the cheapest check that can find it, and reviewers spend their time on judgement, not on what a script can do. Decision rule ¶ Catch a class at the first level that can decide it without judgement, in order of cost: Lint ( tools/preflight.sh , runs in seconds, on every builder's machine). Use it when the defect is a pattern in text or syntax: a forbidden include, a MISRA rule CodeQL reports, a missing else , a parameter name, a symbol named in docs that does not exist, a missing gitlink. Test, model or mutation (host tests, the chip model's fault knobs, fuzz properties, compile-fail cases, mutants of a fix). Use it when the defect is behaviour: what the driver sends or returns when the chip or the bus misbehaves. A test is the right level when the model can be made to misbehave in exactly that way. Independent review question (a reviewer who did not write the code). Use it only for what needs judgement: whether the datasheet was read correctly, whether a state machine is complete, whether the model is independent of the driver, whether a doc claim is true. Every catalogue entry names its level under DETECTION. A class with no lint or test is a review class and costs reviewer time every round; it is a candidate for promotion. Promotion ¶ A defect that reached a reviewer or the CI of a second driver is promoted one level up: review to test, test to lint where a pattern exists. The reviewer who finds the second occurrence writes the promotion item in the round's report; the template maintainer (the agent or person that owns the template branch) implements it before the next driver's first push, or records why it cannot be mechanised in the catalogue entry. A defect that reached a third driver after its promotion means the check is wrong: fix the check first, then look at the driver. Demotion never happens by silence: a check is removed only with a catalogue note saying what replaced it. What a lint may and may not do ¶ It reports file:line , the catalogue id, and the fix. It exits non-zero on a finding, in the preflight and the gate. It has no false-positive tolerance : before merging, it runs over every finished driver and the template; any finding on a driver that CI shows clean is a false positive, and the lint is not merged until it has none (narrow the pattern; do not add an ignore list per driver). It may be conservative the other way (miss cases): then the catalogue says partial and names the review question that covers the rest. It never edits files, never skips silently (a missing tool is reported as a skipped step in the final line, and the gate treats a skipped MISRA or ESP32 step as a failure), and has a selftest with one bad and one good case. It does not replace the CI scan: CI is the final word for MISRA. Recording a new finding ¶ Append the finding to its catalogue entry (driver, review round or CI report file, finding id) and update the count and the index table; add a new entry only when no class fits. Write the check at the level the rules above give: the lint, or the test pattern (model knob, mutant, fuzz property), or the reviewer's question in the skill. Run it over the finished drivers (lint) or add the regression test that fails without the fix (test). Add a CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased] and the template change is released as a new template commit; drivers take it with scaffold.py --check-drift --fix (the skills and tools are managed files), which updates the template pin in .kokeb/template.yml . Mention the catalogue id in the commit subject. The pre-push gate ¶ A driver is cleared for its first push only by kokeb-tools/gate.sh <chip> (the orchestrator's script, one run per driver through the shared Docker lock). It writes a log and a verdict, and PASS needs all of: container preflight ( tools/preflight.sh --container ) with 0 failure(s) and 0 gate failure(s) , including the MISRA scan and the ESP32 builds; a skipped MISRA or ESP32 step is a FAIL; handbook_check reports 0 errors (this includes the library-subset include scan); tools/check_standalone.py passes; template drift: scaffold.py --check-drift reports nothing; no .pdf file is tracked; the examples/esp32/scripts gitlink (mode 160000) is present; the tree is staged as it will be committed. No silent skips: every step prints a line, and a missing tool fails the gate. Roles ¶ Builders write code, models, tests and docs and run host tests and the quick preflight. They do not run the container gate, push, or create repositories. The gate runner is one serialized worker that runs gate.sh for one driver at a time and reports the verdict and the log; it does not edit the driver. Reviewers are read-only and independent. They are given the code, the model, the datasheet, the catalogue and the previous round's report, and never the builder's conclusions (the build report is read only in the claims-vs-code step). They run the review-round protocol. Fixers change the driver, fix at the cause, add the test that fails without the fix, and answer each finding id. The template maintainer applies promotions and keeps the catalogue current. Backlog of promotions (state of the catalogue) ¶ The classes whose target level is above their present level are listed in the catalogue index: RD-12 to RD-18 and RD-23 (MISRA patterns, one misra_lint with a rule per id), RD-20 and RD-22 (ESP-IDF and compile-fail lints), RD-08 ( claims-symbols ), RD-07 (model standalone lint), RD-06, RD-01, RD-02, RD-03, RD-05, RD-10 and RD-25 (shared model knobs and a template mutation runner), RD-21 (host start-up test of the ESP32 port).

Datasheet sections this page relies on Typical application circuit: Worldsemi WS2812B undated, Typical application circuit, p. 5 SK6812RGBW windows, low below 20 us, code period: Opsco SK6812RGBX-XX Rev. 07, 12. The data transmission time, p. 7 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver is platform-free. It builds the byte stream and resolves the waveform; the port turns bytes into pulses. Between the first and the last bit no low may exceed Waveform::max_gap_ticks . A longer low is a reset: the pixels latch what they have and ignore the rest. On a peripheral that refills its buffer from an interrupt, an underrun makes exactly that gap; return false when you can detect one, and log it. The driver cannot detect one itself, and the ESP32 example cannot either. Use DMA or a larger buffer where the part has them. Bit 1: high t1h_ticks , then low t1l_ticks . Bit 0: high t0h_ticks , then low t0l_ticks . Most significant bit first, one byte after the other, no padding bit. The line idles low and ends low , after a frame and after a failure (a frame cut half-way is the reason the driver waits a full reset before the next one). Fit a pull-down on DIN so the line is low before the port drives it (both circuits in Hardware show one at the buffer input). The first symbol of a frame starts high. A line that idles high would be read as the start of a bit. The reset. After the last bit, hold the line low for reset_ticks . A port may do it as a final low symbol, or as a timed wait after the last tick when the symbol field is too short: an RMT half-symbol holds 15 bits, so a reset above 32 767 ticks (1.6 ms at 20 MHz is fine; 300 µs at 20 MHz is 6000 ticks, also fine) needs a wait or several symbols. kRmtHalfSymbolMaxTicks is that limit. The real tick rate. If the peripheral rounds the requested clock, report the rate it got. The driver converts nanoseconds at that rate, and refuses a rate that cannot meet the windows. A timeout. Return false when timeout_ms passes before the frame is out. The driver computes it from the frame time plus Config::transmit_slack_ms . Memory the peripheral reaches. Buffers for DMA live in memory the DMA reaches, owned by the port, never on a caller's stack. Pin idle level. The supply pin starts INACTIVE and is set before it becomes an output (handbook KB-HW-018). ACTIVE means powered; map the polarity in the port. Pin Hook ACTIVE means Idle level Order at start-up Data (DIN) Transmit() n/a low idle low before the channel is enabled Supply enable GpioSet(Power, ...) strip powered INACTIVE (off) set low, then make it an output The ESP32 RMT port ¶ examples/esp32/main/esp32_ws2812_rmt_port.hpp uses the RMT TX driver of ESP-IDF v5.x: one TX channel at 20 MHz (32 MHz on the ESP32-H2), a bytes encoder built from the waveform ( bit0 is high t0h then low t0l , bit1 likewise, most significant bit first), the end-of-transmission level low, and a timed wait for the reset. It is written fresh from the public API. Tick rate per target. The RMT divides its source clock by an integer that ESP-IDF v5.5 rounds to the nearest ( rmt_common.c ), and ResolveRmtRate() computes the same rate. The default source is the 80 MHz APB or PLL clock on the ESP32, S2, S3, C3, C5, C6 and P4, so 20 MHz is exact. The ESP32-H2 runs its RMT from the 32 MHz crystal: 20 MHz is not reachable there (the divider 2 gives 16 MHz, which the port refuses), so the port asks for 32 MHz on that target ( CONFIG_IDF_TARGET_ESP32H2 ). Internal RAM. With CONFIG_RMT_TX_ISR_CACHE_SAFE , rmt_transmit() refuses a payload outside internal RAM, and every Show() or TraceWire() returns Bus . The wire buffer is a member of the driver object, so keep the object out of PSRAM, and pass TraceWire() a span in RAM, not a constant in flash. The frame wait. rmt_tx_wait_all_done() turns its milliseconds into whole RTOS ticks rounded down, and a wait of n ticks can end after n - 1 whole periods, because it starts part-way through the current tick. The port adds two tick periods to the driver's timeout, so the wait is never shorter than timeout_ms , whatever the tick rate and transmit_slack_ms . The rate the channel really got. On the C3, C5, C6, H2, S3 and P4 all RMT channels share one group prescaler ( rmt_common.c , s_rmt_set_group_prescale() ): the first channel created fixes it, and a later channel gets its divider from that group clock. A channel created earlier at another rate (for example an RMT receiver at 1 MHz) can leave this one at a rate the waveform was not computed for, and the pixels would show wrong colours with no error. So after rmt_new_tx_channel() the port reads the real rate ( rmt_get_channel_resolution() , declared in ESP-IDF's internal esp_private/rmt.h ) and refuses to start ( Bus ) when it differs from the computed one. Create this channel first, or give every channel of the group a rate the same group clock reaches. On the host. tests/esp32_stub/ builds this port and both examples against stand-ins of the ESP-IDF headers, runs each example's Start() (the start-up of app_main() ) with the default pins and checks the channel settings, the encoder (bit order and the 32 767-tick limit), the order of the pin and channel calls, the waits, the rate read back and the recovery after a failed transmission. That shows the code paths, not the chip. On parts with RMT DMA, set with_dma in Esp32Ws2812RmtPins . Without DMA the encoder refills the channel memory from an interrupt, so a long strip under interrupt load can underrun; the symptom is a strip that shows the first pixels right and the rest stale or flickering ( Troubleshooting ). How many memory symbols each ESP32 family member has is not verified here: read the soc_caps of your target. Bench steps ¶ None of this is verified on hardware. To confirm a port: send one pixel and a 60-pixel frame, and put a logic analyser or a scope on the data line. Check the pulse widths against the windows of your variant in Timing , the idle level (low), the absence of gaps inside a frame, the reset low time after it, and the tick rate your port reports. Then run a 1024-pixel frame with interrupts busy and look for a gap. Force an aborted frame: make Transmit() time out in the middle of a frame (a very small transmit_slack_ms on a long strip), and check that the line stays low afterwards, that the driver then holds a full reset low, and that the next Show() shows the right colours from the first pixel. The reference port asks the RMT for mem_block_symbols symbols: 0 picks two memory blocks without DMA (a multiple of SOC_RMT_MEM_WORDS_PER_CHANNEL : 128 on the ESP32 and ESP32-S2, 96 on the ESP32-C3, C6, H2 and S3) and 1024 with DMA. These are the SOC_RMT_MEM_WORDS_PER_CHANNEL values of the ESP-IDF v5.5 soc_caps.h files (64 words on the ESP32 and S2, 48 on the others), not checked on a chip. The interrupt priority is 3 ( Esp32Ws2812RmtPins::intr_priority ), also unverified.

Datasheet sections this page relies on From Worldsemi WS2812B-V5 V5.0: Pins and package: four pin 5050: PIN Configuration, p. 2 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . 1. Wire it ¶ MCU Strip Notes Timed-output pin (on ESP32 an RMT channel) DIN A 5 V strip needs a level shifter for a 3.3 V MCU: see Hardware GPIO (optional) Supply enable Only if you want PowerOn() and PowerOff() GND GND Common ground with the strip supply VDD 5 V supply with a large capacitor at the strip input and 100 nF at each pixel 2. Add the driver ¶ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-ws2812-rmt.git external/driver-ws2812-rmt 3. Write the port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyPort : public ws2812_rmt :: GpioInterface < MyPort > { public : // Create and enable the channel once; the line idles low. Later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_tx_open ( kDataGpio , ws2812_rmt :: kRecommendedResolutionHz ); } return ready_ ; } // The rate the channel really runs at, not the one you asked for. bool ResolutionHz ( uint32_t & hz ) noexcept { hz = platform_tx_rate (); return hz != 0U ; } // Send every byte, most significant bit first, as one gapless stream, then hold the line low for // wave.reset_ticks. Return when the last tick is out, or false on a failure or a timeout (leave // the line low: the driver then waits a full reset through DelayUs() before the next frame). bool Transmit ( std :: span < const uint8_t > wire , const ws2812_rmt :: Waveform & wave , uint32_t timeout_ms ) noexcept { return platform_tx_send ( wire . data (), static_cast < uint32_t > ( wire . size ()), wave , timeout_ms ); } // A wait with the line low. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : static constexpr int32_t kDataGpio = 4 ; bool ready_ = false ; }; On ESP32 use the finished port in examples/esp32 instead. 4. Show a colour ¶ main.cpp #include "ws2812_rmt.hpp" // 60 pixels of a current WS2812B (V5 or later): the default variant, GRB order. int32_t light_first_pixel_red () { MyPort port ; ws2812_rmt :: Ws2812Rmt < MyPort , 60 > strip ( port ); // owns the pixel and wire buffers; no I/O yet if ( auto r = strip . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 1. channel up, waveform resolved at the real rate return static_cast < int32_t > ( r . error ); // Bus, or TimingUnreachable for an unsuitable rate } strip . Clear (); // 2. all pixels black static_cast < void > ( strip . SetPixel ( 0 , ws2812_rmt :: Colour { 255 , 0 , 0 , 0 })); // pixel 0 is the first if ( auto r = strip . Show (); ! r ) { // 3. encode, send, wait for the reset return static_cast < int32_t > ( r . error ); // Bus: the frame was not sent } return 0 ; } EnsureInitialized() creates the channel through your port, asks it for its real tick rate and resolves the waveform. A rate that cannot meet the datasheet windows is refused here ( TimingUnreachable ). SetPixel() and Fill() only store colours. Show() encodes them and sends the frame. The defaults suit a current WS2812B (V5 or V6, GRB). For another part set Config::variant : Timing says which one to pick. Next: API guide .

docs.text: Recurring defects ¶ The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver. lint lint Chip-protocol and safety classes ¶ RD-01 Write after an unseen device reset ¶ Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?" RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read ¶ Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?" RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data ¶ Rule: a reply a dead, shorted or floating line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never a measurement or a ready status. // bad: an all-zero frame has a valid CRC for init 0x00, so 0 degC (or -200 degC after the offset) is returned auto t = DecodeTemperature ( words ); // good: reject by pattern before decoding, then plausibility-check the decoded value if ( IsStuck ( words )) { return Error :: NoDevice ; } Hurts: a wrong value is returned as data, which downstream control trusts. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J3), tmc5160 (review1 M8), sfm (review3 M-A: the temperature path had no stuck check while the sample path had one). 3 drivers. Detection: test : one model fault per pattern (zeros, ones, echo, repeat) applied to every read function; a table test lists each public read function and the fault, so a new read function without a row fails. review : hardware-lessons-review 4. Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?" RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something ¶ Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?" RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused ¶ Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends." RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack ¶ Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?" RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading ¶ Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?" RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard ¶ Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?" RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard ¶ Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?" RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read ¶ Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Seen: pf1550 (review1 M2: SelfCheck() and ReadRegister() read status registers the chip clears on read), tmc5160 (review1: Service() cleared the stall event, a BLOCKER, review1 B1). 2 drivers. Detection: test : model with clear-on-read bits; test reads through every diagnostic path, then asserts the latch still reports the fault. review : hardware-lessons-review 10, 12b. Datasheet and documentation classes ¶ RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing ¶ Rule: every field position, clear semantic, wait and gap cites its section and has a test that pins it independently. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1, J4), tmc5160 (review1 B1), sfm (review1 M3, M4), ws2812 (review1 M2, M3), fdo2 (review1 M3, M4). 6 drivers. Detection: review (datasheet-conformance): re-derive the five facts the change touches from the datasheet before reading the code. Question: "For this register or frame, what do the datasheet's bits say, and does the code agree before you look at the model?" RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit ¶ Rule: a reference circuit, wiring table or example never exceeds an absolute maximum or ties a pin the datasheet forbids tying. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M7), fdo2 (review1 M9), ws2812 (review1 M3: documents disagree on the input threshold). 3 drivers. Detection: review : docs and diagram pass. Question: "For each net in the reference circuit, what is the highest voltage the chip pin sees, and where does the datasheet allow it?" RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks ¶ Rule: every behavioural claim in docs, Doxygen, the contract and the build report is checked against the code line that implements it and the test that pins it. /// Enables the bridge again. // doc Result < void > ClearFaults (); // code returns Busy while the motor moves and stays disabled Hurts: callers and later reviewers rely on the claim; a promised error never occurs, a promised recovery never runs. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M5, review2 N2, n9), tmc5160 (review1 M4, review5 m1), fdo2 (review1 M7), pf1550 (review1 M6), bno08x (review1 M-1), ads9324 (review1 J5-J7). 6 drivers. Detection: review via the review-round claims-vs-code check: list every "always", "never", "returns", "enables" in docs and the build report and cite the code line and test for each. Mechanical part ( lint , planned): every Error named in docs exists; every Doxygen @return lists the values the function can return. RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim ¶ Rule: a matrix row, test id or knob named in docs exists in code, and a row's test asserts the row. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J5, J6: 873 rows unproved, fuzz claims invariants it does not check), pf1550 (review2 F4: 47 rows cite symbols that do not exist; F5: knobs that do not exist; review1 M11), ws2812 (review2 n9: "each fix has a test" overstated). 3 drivers. Detection: lint (planned claims-symbols ): every backticked identifier in the datasheet coverage page, the coverage matrix and docs/ambiguities.md resolves with grep in inc/ src/ tests/ . review : row-level sample. RD-32 Docs style ¶ Rule: Markdown lines are at most 120 characters, list items are separated, text changed by a fix is updated everywhere. Seen: ws2812 (review2 n4, n5, n6), ntc (review1), mcp9700 (review2 m2-1). 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced : markdownlint in the preflight; line length 120). Stale text after a change is RD-09. RD-33 Another project's name or dated history ¶ Seen: ntc (review1 M5: old-history wording in eleven places). 1 driver; enforced by tools/check_standalone.py . Process and test-quality classes ¶ RD-25 Guards no test kills ¶ Rule: every guard that protects a write, a state or a value has a test that fails when the guard is removed. Seen: ads9324 (review1 mutants M22 to N66), pf1550 (review2 F3, review3 N4, review4 R4-2: 7 of 12 survivors matter, review5 R5-1), tmc5160 (review1 M6: 22 of 50 survive), bno08x (review1 M-3: 33 survive), alicat (review2, review3). 6 drivers. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes. RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules ¶ Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?" RD-34 Unspecified evaluation order in a test check ¶ Rule: a call in a test or fuzz target takes, as separate arguments, no operation that changes state together with a read of that state ( sent() , Transfers() , pending() , a flag, a counter, a clock). The order of the arguments of a call, of the operands of + - == < and of the two sides of an assignment is unspecified; GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left, Clang and GCC on aarch64 left to right. Braced-init lists, && , || , ?: and , are sequenced. Two reads of the fuzzer's input ( in.Byte() , FuzzConfig(in) ) in one expression count as well: they advance the input, so the same corpus file decodes into different calls per compiler. // bad: x86-64 GCC reads sent() before the call, so it is always 0 here Check ( d . Write ( v ), was_up , sent ()); // good: the result first, then the read; or pass the probe and read it inside the helper, after the call const auto r = d . Write ( v ); Check ( r , was_up , sent ()); Hurts: the check passes, or aborts, on one CI runner only. A "nothing was sent" promise becomes vacuous, and a positive promise ( sent >= 1 ) aborts on a correct driver; neither shows on an Apple-silicon or aarch64 rehearsal. Seen: dynamixel (first CI, sent >= 1 aborted on x86-64 GCC only), pcal9555 (three fuzz cases, latent), tle92466ed (16 fuzz cases, vacuous; 6 more with two input reads), the template's own fuzz target (5 cases). 3 drivers, all copies of the same pattern. Detection: lint ( enforced ): tools/eval_order_check.py , the eval-order preflight step, scans tests/ and examples/ . test : the fuzz replay with a one-edit mutant that must abort ( mutant_replay_* , kept out of the fuzz_* names so the libFuzzer job does not pick it up). RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule ¶ Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit. RD-19 Template drift ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate. RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI ¶ Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count). CI-only checks (MISRA scan, ESP-IDF, compile-fail) ¶ RD-11 Header outside the library subset ¶ Rule: #include <...> in inc/ and src/ is only from the driver subset of the handbook (KB-CPP-012). #include <numeric> // bad: not in the subset; std::accumulate -> write the OR out #include <string_view> Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt , <string_view> ), tmc5160 (review4 B1, <numeric> ). 2 drivers; the second hit makes it a lint. Detection: lint ( enforced in handbook_check; the preflight must also run the include scan or grep). RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic ¶ Rule: no arithmetic or comparison on a char value, including c - '0' and c == 'x' . int d = c - '0' ; // bad if ( c == 'A' ) {} // bad const int d = DigitValue ( c ); // good: lookup in a constexpr digit array via std::find Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : the bare comparisons too), alicat (review2: about 30 computations predicted; review3 R3-M1, six conversions; m-10, tests), pf1550 (review4 m-4: a template file used in tests). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 7.0.3 (planned): char literals in arithmetic or comparison in inc src tests examples . Until then: grep '.' next to - , + , == , != . RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses ¶ Rule: a binary operand that is itself a binary expression of higher precedence is parenthesised, in static_assert too. static_assert ( kA == 1 && kB < 2 ); // bad static_assert (( kA == 1 ) && ( kB < 2 )); // good Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt , three lines), pf1550 (review4 m-1: static_assert s). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 8.0.1 (planned): parenthesis-depth scan of inc src tests . RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain ¶ Rule: every if ... else if chain ends with else , with a comment when empty; in tests and models too. Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci3.txt ), tmc5160 (review5 B1: two chains in the model). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 9.4.1 (planned). RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : failInit ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 0.1.2 (planned): a call to a non-void function as an expression statement; mark with an explicit discard where intended. RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : checkOxygen ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 13.3.3 (planned): declaration in inc/ against definition in src/*.ipp . RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type ¶ Rule: a constant argument has its parameter's type ( _u32 literal), and no mixed-width arithmetic on literals. Seen: ntc (review1 M3), fdo2 (review1 M10), tmc5160 (review1 M7), ws2812 (review1: call sites). 4 drivers. Detection: lint (partial, planned): literal passed to a uint32_t or uint8_t parameter of a known function; review for the rest (the CI scan is final). Question: "Which call passes a bare integer constant to a narrower parameter?" RD-18 Advisories 6.9.2, 15.1.4, 0.0.2 ¶ Rule: these three appear on every driver and need no re-report: 6.9.2 on the unsigned long long literal-operator parameter and on the version getters, 15.1.4 on a constructor whose members have default initialisers, 0.0.2 on a condition a constant-hook port makes always the same. Seen in CI: fdo2, ads9324 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ); predicted by the reviewer from those runs: pf1550 (review3, review4 m-4), alicat (review3, review4), bno08x (review1). 5 drivers. Detection: lint (planned): the gate compares the CodeQL advisory list to this known list; anything else is new. Reviewers do not report the known three; whether to record them as deviations is an owner decision. RD-20 ESP-IDF REQUIRES incomplete ¶ Rule: every #include of an ESP-IDF header in examples/esp32/main has its component in REQUIRES . Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : esp_timer.h ; the ESP32 job failed in both examples). Later reviews found it clean ( pf1550 review5). 1 driver. Detection: lint (planned): include-to-component map checked against the idf_component_register call. RD-21 ESP32 example cannot start with its defaults ¶ Rule: the example's default pins and Config start up; an optional hook returns true when the pin is absent. Seen: fdo2 (review1 M5), mcp9700 (review1 B-1: GpioSet returned false with the default -1 pin), ntc (review1 M1). 3 drivers. Detection: test : build the ESP32 port against stub ESP headers on the host and run the example's start-up with default Config . review : question "does app_main with the default pins reach the first measurement?" RD-22 Compile-fail regex wording differs by compiler ¶ Rule: an EXPECT: is a concept or type name, or the static_assert text, never compiler wording. Seen: no CI failure yet. Reviewers could not confirm GCC 13/14 and clang CI wording for alicat, pf1550, bno08x (review4, review5, review1). 0 driver hits; listed because it is unverified each time. Detection: lint (planned): every EXPECT: string is static assertion failed , an identifier, or a string from a static_assert . RD-23 Tests are also scanned by MISRA ¶ Rule: the MISRA job builds with tests on, so tests/ , models, fuzz and consumers meet the same rules as inc/ . Seen: tmc5160 (review5 B1, the model), alicat (review3 m-10: char compares in tests and the model, "if CodeQL scans tests"). 2 drivers; whether the job reports test files is not proved by the two CI runs on file. Detection: lint : every misra_lint rule scans tests/ examples/ as well as inc/ src/ .
docs.title: Recurring defects

docs.text: The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver.
