docs.title: Index

docs.text: Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?"
docs.title: RD-01 Write after an unseen device reset

docs.text: Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?"
docs.title: RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read

docs.text: Rule: a reply a dead, shorted or floating line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never a measurement or a ready status. // bad: an all-zero frame has a valid CRC for init 0x00, so 0 degC (or -200 degC after the offset) is returned auto t = DecodeTemperature ( words ); // good: reject by pattern before decoding, then plausibility-check the decoded value if ( IsStuck ( words )) { return Error :: NoDevice ; } Hurts: a wrong value is returned as data, which downstream control trusts. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J3), tmc5160 (review1 M8), sfm (review3 M-A: the temperature path had no stuck check while the sample path had one). 3 drivers. Detection: test : one model fault per pattern (zeros, ones, echo, repeat) applied to every read function; a table test lists each public read function and the fault, so a new read function without a row fails. review : hardware-lessons-review 4. Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?"
docs.title: RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data

docs.text: Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?"
docs.title: RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something

docs.text: Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends."
docs.title: RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused

docs.text: Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?"
docs.title: RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack

docs.text: Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?"
docs.title: RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading

docs.text: Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?"
docs.title: RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard

docs.text: Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?"
docs.title: RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard

docs.text: Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Seen: pf1550 (review1 M2: SelfCheck() and ReadRegister() read status registers the chip clears on read), tmc5160 (review1: Service() cleared the stall event, a BLOCKER, review1 B1). 2 drivers. Detection: test : model with clear-on-read bits; test reads through every diagnostic path, then asserts the latch still reports the fault. review : hardware-lessons-review 10, 12b.
docs.title: RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read

docs.text: Rule: every field position, clear semantic, wait and gap cites its section and has a test that pins it independently. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1, J4), tmc5160 (review1 B1), sfm (review1 M3, M4), ws2812 (review1 M2, M3), fdo2 (review1 M3, M4). 6 drivers. Detection: review (datasheet-conformance): re-derive the five facts the change touches from the datasheet before reading the code. Question: "For this register or frame, what do the datasheet's bits say, and does the code agree before you look at the model?"
docs.title: RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing

docs.text: Rule: a reference circuit, wiring table or example never exceeds an absolute maximum or ties a pin the datasheet forbids tying. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M7), fdo2 (review1 M9), ws2812 (review1 M3: documents disagree on the input threshold). 3 drivers. Detection: review : docs and diagram pass. Question: "For each net in the reference circuit, what is the highest voltage the chip pin sees, and where does the datasheet allow it?"
docs.title: RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit

docs.text: Rule: every behavioural claim in docs, Doxygen, the contract and the build report is checked against the code line that implements it and the test that pins it. /// Enables the bridge again. // doc Result < void > ClearFaults (); // code returns Busy while the motor moves and stays disabled Hurts: callers and later reviewers rely on the claim; a promised error never occurs, a promised recovery never runs. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M5, review2 N2, n9), tmc5160 (review1 M4, review5 m1), fdo2 (review1 M7), pf1550 (review1 M6), bno08x (review1 M-1), ads9324 (review1 J5-J7). 6 drivers. Detection: review via the review-round claims-vs-code check: list every "always", "never", "returns", "enables" in docs and the build report and cite the code line and test for each. Mechanical part ( lint , planned): every Error named in docs exists; every Doxygen @return lists the values the function can return.
docs.title: RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks

docs.text: Rule: a matrix row, test id or knob named in docs exists in code, and a row's test asserts the row. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J5, J6: 873 rows unproved, fuzz claims invariants it does not check), pf1550 (review2 F4: 47 rows cite symbols that do not exist; F5: knobs that do not exist; review1 M11), ws2812 (review2 n9: "each fix has a test" overstated). 3 drivers. Detection: lint (planned claims-symbols ): every backticked identifier in the datasheet coverage page, the coverage matrix and docs/ambiguities.md resolves with grep in inc/ src/ tests/ . review : row-level sample.
docs.title: RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim

docs.text: Rule: Markdown lines are at most 120 characters, list items are separated, text changed by a fix is updated everywhere. Seen: ws2812 (review2 n4, n5, n6), ntc (review1), mcp9700 (review2 m2-1). 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced : markdownlint in the preflight; line length 120). Stale text after a change is RD-09.
docs.title: RD-32 Docs style

docs.text: Seen: ntc (review1 M5: old-history wording in eleven places). 1 driver; enforced by tools/check_standalone.py .
docs.title: RD-33 Another project's name or dated history

docs.text: Rule: every guard that protects a write, a state or a value has a test that fails when the guard is removed. Seen: ads9324 (review1 mutants M22 to N66), pf1550 (review2 F3, review3 N4, review4 R4-2: 7 of 12 survivors matter, review5 R5-1), tmc5160 (review1 M6: 22 of 50 survive), bno08x (review1 M-3: 33 survive), alicat (review2, review3). 6 drivers. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes.
docs.title: RD-25 Guards no test kills

docs.text: Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?"
docs.title: RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules

docs.text: Rule: a call in a test or fuzz target takes, as separate arguments, no operation that changes state together with a read of that state ( sent() , Transfers() , pending() , a flag, a counter, a clock). The order of the arguments of a call, of the operands of + - == < and of the two sides of an assignment is unspecified; GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left, Clang and GCC on aarch64 left to right. Braced-init lists, && , || , ?: and , are sequenced. Two reads of the fuzzer's input ( in.Byte() , FuzzConfig(in) ) in one expression count as well: they advance the input, so the same corpus file decodes into different calls per compiler. // bad: x86-64 GCC reads sent() before the call, so it is always 0 here Check ( d . Write ( v ), was_up , sent ()); // good: the result first, then the read; or pass the probe and read it inside the helper, after the call const auto r = d . Write ( v ); Check ( r , was_up , sent ()); Hurts: the check passes, or aborts, on one CI runner only. A "nothing was sent" promise becomes vacuous, and a positive promise ( sent >= 1 ) aborts on a correct driver; neither shows on an Apple-silicon or aarch64 rehearsal. Seen: dynamixel (first CI, sent >= 1 aborted on x86-64 GCC only), pcal9555 (three fuzz cases, latent), tle92466ed (16 fuzz cases, vacuous; 6 more with two input reads), the template's own fuzz target (5 cases). 3 drivers, all copies of the same pattern. Detection: lint ( enforced ): tools/eval_order_check.py , the eval-order preflight step, scans tests/ and examples/ . test : the fuzz replay with a one-edit mutant that must abort ( mutant_replay_* , kept out of the fuzz_* names so the libFuzzer job does not pick it up).
docs.title: RD-34 Unspecified evaluation order in a test check

docs.text: Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit.
docs.title: RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate.
docs.title: RD-19 Template drift

docs.text: Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count).

docs.text: Rule: #include <...> in inc/ and src/ is only from the driver subset of the handbook (KB-CPP-012). #include <numeric> // bad: not in the subset; std::accumulate -> write the OR out #include <string_view> Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt , <string_view> ), tmc5160 (review4 B1, <numeric> ). 2 drivers; the second hit makes it a lint. Detection: lint ( enforced in handbook_check; the preflight must also run the include scan or grep).

docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply ; --org names the organisation (a driver lives in kokeb-labs-drivers , everything else in kokeb-labs ) and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( spi eeprom microchip at25040b ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> # the plan python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, Actions, labels, ... A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it again, with --check to see that nothing is pending, after the repository goes public (section 6). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ --apply in step 2 already creates them; this is the manual way, for a repository outside the org tool. python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md . 6. First release candidate and going public ¶ The order that works, and the reason for each step: main green first. Push, and wait for CI on main , including CI gate / gate . The docs publish to gh-pages from main before any tag does. Triage a failure with the release skill, section 5: re-run the failed jobs only when the infrastructure failed. Tag vX.Y.Z-rc.1 on that commit (the release skill). Its CI repeats the run, then the Release workflow publishes the pre-release: firmware, SBOM, checksums. A pre-release publishes its docs under its own tag and takes latest only when no other version holds it. Make it public ( gh repo edit <org>/<repo> --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences ), then python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply : rulesets, secret scanning with push protection, CodeQL and private vulnerability reporting need a public repository. If the last call answers 422, run it again after a few seconds; the new visibility has not reached that endpoint yet. Enable Pages from the gh-pages branch, root, and open https://<org>.github.io/<repo>/ . --check reports 0 change(s) pending . A private repository on the free plan shares a small Actions storage quota with the rest of its organisation. A full quota fails every upload step in every repository of it at once, which looks like a broken workflow and is not one; a public repository does not count against it.

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against a model of the pixels written from the datasheets, a fuzzer that controls the configuration, the tick rate and the port's failures, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. Host tests ¶ cmake -S . -B build -DWS2812_RMT_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_waveform.cpp ResolveWaveform() at known rates, the edges of every window, the period, reset and gap-limit rules, ResolveRmtRate() (the divider arithmetic of the ESP32 port), a sweep of hostile rates tests/test_timing_models.cpp Every profile equals the intersection of its documents; the nominals lie inside every document; two WS2812B generations share no waveform; default orders tests/test_model.cpp The model itself: its decoding, its windows, its latch, with hand-made symbol streams tests/test_encode.cpp , test_colour.cpp Byte packing for every colour order, Scale8 over all 65 536 pairs, gamma, white, wheel tests/test_frame.cpp Frame time, refresh rate, pixels per frame, the input-level function tests/test_chain.cpp End to end: every variant, every document, every order, strips of 1 to 1024 pixels, a tick-rate error of 1000 ppm tests/test_lifecycle.cpp , test_errors.cpp , test_bus_faults.cpp Start-up, every error value, failing and underrunning ports tests/test_edges.cpp The boundaries a one-edit change would move: the reset wait at a rate that is not whole megahertz, the rounded-up tick time, the longer bit code in the frame time, the exclusive in-frame cap, the recovery after a failed PowerOff() tests/esp32_stub/ The ESP32 port and both examples over stand-ins of the ESP-IDF headers: each example's Start() with the default pins reaches a shown frame, the channel settings, encoder, waits and recovery, the ESP32-H2 default rate tests/test_kconfig.cpp The menuconfig values and their defaults tests/mock_ws2812_rmt.hpp The model: the documents' windows, a pixel chain that latches, and the fake ports tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( ws2812_rmt_fuzz_ws2812_rmt_corpus ), see below tests/compile_fail/ Ports and configurations that must not compile tests/docs/ Every code block of the site, compiled tests/check_install.cmake find_package(ws2812_rmt) from an installed package The tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. What a test cannot show on the host ¶ Every behaviour fix of the review rounds has a host test that fails without it, except these, which a host cannot exercise. Documentation, label and figure fixes, the typed constants (checked by the compiler) and the reset-wait busy loop are reviewed, not tested: The ESP32 port on the chip (the real clock, the memory size, the interrupt priority, the line level after a timeout) needs ESP-IDF and a chip. On the host, tests/esp32_stub/ builds the port and both examples against stand-ins of the ESP-IDF headers and runs each example's start-up, the channel settings, the encoder, the waits and the recovery; its divider arithmetic is the pure ResolveRmtRate() , which is tested on its own as well. Whether the RMT driver reports an underrun is a property of ESP-IDF: the docs state that this port cannot see one, and the model test of an underrun shows the silent outcome a port that cannot see it produces. The reference circuit figures ( docs/hardware.yml ) are checked by kokeb-docs hardware --check and kokeb-docs figures --check for validity and routing, not for electrical correctness. The model stands alone ¶ tests/mock_ws2812_rmt.hpp carries its own table of the windows of each datasheet document ( kDocuments ), typed in from the PDFs and never from the driver's profile table. A test cross-checks that every named variant is the intersection of its documents. The pixel chain decodes the half-symbols the port was given into bits, judges every duration against the window, latches a frame when a low exceeds the reset, and reports pixels that received too few or too many bits. So a transcription error in either table, a waveform outside a window, or a missing reset fails a test, and green tests cannot come from one author's single reading of a datasheet. Fuzz tests ¶ tests/fuzz/fuzz_ws2812_rmt.cpp lets libFuzzer choose a configuration (any variant, Custom with arbitrary windows, any order, brightness, gamma, reset), the port (any tick rate including 0 and 2^32 - 1, failing hooks, with or without the optional hooks) and up to 48 driver calls. After every call it checks the driver's promises and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks: a failed call returns an Error this driver returns (never Timeout , Crc or Busy ) and T{} ; before EnsureInitialized() succeeded the port saw no Transmit() , and InvalidArgument , NotInitialized and TimingUnreachable mean nothing was transmitted; every transmitted waveform lies inside the windows of the declared profile and its reset is above the minimum: a hostile tick rate can never produce an illegal waveform; the wire has exactly Length() x channels bytes at every Transmit() , equal to a second encoding written in the target; after a failed Transmit() the pixels are intact, and the port's waits before the next Transmit() add up to strictly more than the reset (the port records every DelayUs() and every Transmit() in order); the supply pin write fails when the input says so: a failed write is Bus , PowerOn() then leaves the strip as it was, and after any PowerOff() (also one whose write failed) Show() and TraceWire() transmit nothing and return NotPowered ; TraceWire() sends exactly the bytes it was given, and an empty span or one above four bytes per pixel of capacity is InvalidArgument with nothing sent; every log line is a non-empty plain-text message. # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DWS2812_RMT_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DWS2812_RMT_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_ws2812_rmt ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_ws2812_rmt -max_total_time = 120 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_ws2812_rmt The same file also builds without libFuzzer as fuzz_replay_fuzz_ws2812_rmt , and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_ws2812_rmt/ on GCC and Clang ( ws2812_rmt_fuzz_ws2812_rmt_corpus ): the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise (name it regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. CI fuzzes for 120 s on every pull request, from the seeds plus a corpus it keeps between runs (job Host quality / fuzz ). Quality gates ¶ The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Measured on the last run: lines 97.2 % (522 of 537), functions 93.9 %, branches 89.1 % (344 of 386), conditions 88.9 % (304 of 342), decisions 84.2 % (133 of 158). | Sanitizers | Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest | no report | | Fuzzing | libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 120 s per target | no broken promise | The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DWS2812_RMT_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DWS2812_RMT_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( ws2812_rmt_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/ws2812_rmt.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published. CI workflows ¶ Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml with the repository root as the driver's component. The gate needs it too.

Datasheet sections this page relies on WS2812 (6 pin) windows: Worldsemi WS2812 undated, Data transfer time, p. 4 WS2812B 2013 windows: Worldsemi WS2812B undated, Data transfer time, p. 3 WS2812B Mar-2017 windows: Worldsemi WS2812B Mar-2017, Data Transfer Time, p. 4 T0H, T0L, T1H, T1L windows: WS2812B V5, V6, 2020: Worldsemi WS2812B-V5 V5.0, Data Transfer Time, p. 3 RES: the reset low time: Worldsemi WS2812B-V5 V5.0, Data Transfer Time (RES), p. 3 Propagation delay DIN to DOUT: Worldsemi WS2812B-V5 V5.0, Switching Characteristics, p. 3 Cascade and data transmission method: Worldsemi WS2812B-V5 V5.0, Data Transmission Method, p. 4 Same windows, V6 edition: Worldsemi WS2812B-V6 V1.1, Data Transfer Time, p. 4 WS2812C windows: Worldsemi WS2812C V1.0, Data Transfer Time, p. 3 WS2812D-F8 windows: Worldsemi WS2812D-F8 V1.1, Data Transfer Time, p. 4 SK6812 windows: Opsco SK6812 Rev. 01, Data transfer time, p. 5 Reset low time of the SK6812: Opsco SK6812 Rev. 01, Data transfer time (Trst), p. 5 SK6812RGBW windows, low below 20 us, code period: Opsco SK6812RGBX-XX Rev. 07, 12. The bit ¶ A bit is a high pulse followed by a low one, and the length of the high pulse is the value: a short high is 0, a long high is 1. The data line idles low. After the last bit of the frame the line stays low for the reset time, which latches the colours. Symbol Meaning T0H, T0L 0 code: high time, low time T1H, T1L 1 code: high time, low time RES Low time, above which the pixels latch and the next bit starts a new frame Each datasheet gives a window (a minimum and a maximum) for each of the four times, sometimes a bit period, and a minimum for RES. The windows are not the same across parts or even across revisions of one part. The WS2812B has four generations (2013, Mar-2017, V5, V6) whose windows have no waveform in common : the T1L of the Mar-2017 sheet is 220 to 420 ns, and the T1L of V5 is 580 ns to 1 µs. Pick the variant of your LEDs ¶ Config::variant selects one set of windows. Each named variant is the intersection of the windows of every document of that variant, so a waveform inside it satisfies all of them. Variant Parts Reset above Documents (id of the map ) Ws2812bV5 (default) WS2812B V5 and V6, WS2812B-2020, WS2812C-2020 280 µs b-v5, b-v5-w, b-v6-h, b-v6, b-2020, c-2020, b-1313 Ws2812bPreV5 WS2812B of 2013 to 2017, WS2812S 300 µs; low inside a frame below 50 µs b-af, b-cn, b-mar17, ws2812s Ws2812 WS2812 (6 pin) 50 µs ws2812 Ws2812c WS2812C (5050), WS2812-2020 280 µs c-a, c-b, ws-2020 Ws2812d WS2812D-F8 280 µs d-f8 Sk6812 SK6812 (RGB) 80 µs; low inside a frame below 50 µs sk-01 Sk6812Rgbw SK6812RGBW 80 µs; low inside a frame below 20 µs skw-01, skw-03, skw-07 Sk6812Mini SK6812MINI, MINI-E 80 µs; low inside a frame below 20 µs skm-e; skm (windows only) Custom any other part with this frame your value yours How to tell a WS2812B generation: the V5 and V6 sheets say "Ver. No." and show a reset of 280 µs, T1H and T1L of 580 ns to 1 µs; older sheets show 300 ± 150 ns style values and a reset of 50 or 300 µs. The date of the datasheet you bought the strip with, or the silkscreen revision, is the guide. A strip that flickers or shows wrong colours with the default variant usually wants Ws2812bPreV5 . WaveformInWindow(variant, wave) checks one waveform against one variant's windows: mixed chains . The Ws2812bPreV5 bit period is limited to 950 to 1550 ns, not the 650 to 1850 ns of the 2013 sheets: the WS2812S sheet prints 1.25 µs +-300 ns and its documents are part of the variant. The profile is the intersection, so the tighter period applies. The windows of every document are in the model of the tests, tests/mock_ws2812_rmt.hpp ( kDocuments ), which is written from the datasheets and kept apart from the driver's profile table, so that a transcription error in either shows up as a test failure. How a waveform is resolved ¶ EnsureInitialized() asks the port for its real tick rate and calls ResolveWaveform() : timing.cpp // What the driver does at start-up, by hand: nanoseconds into ticks at the port's real rate. bool WaveformFor20Mhz () { const auto wave = ws2812_rmt :: ResolveWaveform ( ws2812_rmt :: ProfileTiming ( ws2812_rmt :: Variant :: Ws2812bV5 ), 20'000'000 , 0 ); if ( ! wave ) { return false ; // TimingUnreachable } // A 20 MHz tick is 50 ns: T0H 7 ticks (350 ns), T0L 19, T1H 14, T1L 12, reset 6000 ticks (300 // us). return ( wave . value . t0h_ticks == 7U ) && ( wave . value . reset_ticks == 6000U ); } Each duration is converted to ticks: the smallest tick count at or above the window minimum, the largest at or below the maximum. The edges are inclusive. The aim is the nominal value of the profile, clamped to the window. If no tick count fits a window (the tick is longer than the window), the result is TimingUnreachable , and nothing is sent. The driver also refuses a named variant at a rate below kMinResolutionHz (20 MHz): see Why 20 MHz . A period minimum (the V6 data cycle of 1250 ns, the SK6812 code period of 1200 ns) is met by lengthening the low of a bit, which stays inside its window. The reset is strictly above the minimum: Config::reset_us , or the datasheet minimum plus 20 µs when it is 0. The reset is a timed low after the last bit: the ESP32 port waits it with the line idle low ( eot_level ), so no RMT symbol has to hold it and the 32 767-tick half-symbol limit does not apply to it. The longest low inside a frame, max_gap_ticks , is the smallest latch time any document of the variant prints, less 10 percent, and strictly below that: 252 µs for V5 (latch above 280 µs), 45 µs for the 2013 WS2812B and the SK6812 (their sheets print a 50 µs latch next to the larger reset the driver sends), 18 µs for SK6812RGBW and MINI (the sheet says the low must stay below 20 µs). The port must not leave a gap that long inside a frame, or the pixels latch half a frame. The reset the driver sends is the larger value, which every generation accepts. The V5 nominals at 20 MHz are 7 ticks for T0H, 19 for T0L, and 13 each for T1H and T1L (350, 950, 650 and 650 ns). The tick rate must be the real one: the port reports what the peripheral runs at, and the driver converts at that rate. Why V5 aims T0H at 350 ns ¶ The V5 window of T0H is 220 to 380 ns (the sheets print windows, no typical value; its centre is 300 ns), but the V6 sheet adds a data cycle of at least 1250 ns (T0H + T0L and T1H + T1L). The Ws2812bV5 profile covers V6, so the cycle applies. With T0H 300 ns and T0L 950 ns (19 ticks of 50 ns) the cycle is exactly 1250 ns: any clock error below nominal shortens it under the limit (at +1000 ppm 1248.75 ns). With T0H 350 ns (7 ticks) the cycle is 1300 ns, 4 % above the minimum, while T0H keeps 30 ns of margin below its 380 ns maximum and T0L 50 ns below its 1000 ns maximum. 350 and 950 ns are the best pair for the 0 code at 20 MHz: no other tick pair beats 30 ns of margin on every edge. The 1 code is 650 + 650 = 1300 ns as well, 70 ns from both window edges, so every bit takes 1300 ns and a strip of 1024 pixels still meets the 30 frames per second of the sheets. The test A tick-rate error of +-1000 ppm stays inside every window fails with 300 ns. Thin margins that remain at 20 MHz, against the printed windows: 30 ns on the V5 profile (T0H; the 1300 ns bit is 50 ns above the 1250 ns cycle), 50 ns on the 2013 to 2017 WS2812B, SK6812RGBW and SK6812MINI profiles, 70 ns on WS2812C and 80 ns on WS2812D. A clock within 1000 ppm moves an edge by about 1 ns, so none of them leaves its window. Why 20 MHz ¶ At 10 MHz a tick is 100 ns. The T0H window of V5 (220 to 380 ns) then holds a single tick count (300 ns), and a bit period of 1250 ns can only be met with T0L at the very edge of its window (1000 ns): the margin is 0 ns, and a clock error of 1000 ppm leaves the window (the same holds at 8, 9.6 and 12 MHz). At 16 MHz V5 still sits exactly on an edge, and the rates between 16 and 20 MHz leave no margin to spare either. At 20 MHz (50 ns ticks) every window holds several tick counts, so the aimed values sit 30 ns or more from the edges and a clock error of 1000 ppm cannot push them out. kRecommendedResolutionHz and kMinResolutionHz are both 20 MHz (a finer rate such as 40 MHz or 80 MHz keeps the margins), and the driver returns TimingUnreachable below it for a named variant ( Custom is not limited: its windows are yours). Frame time ¶ The time of a frame is pixels x bits per pixel x the longer bit period , plus the reset. FrameTimeNs() , MaxRefreshHz() and MaxPixelsAtRate() compute it from a waveform: timing.cpp // How many pixels fit in a 30 Hz refresh, and what a 60-pixel frame costs. void FrameBudget () { const auto wave = ws2812_rmt :: ResolveWaveform ( ws2812_rmt :: ProfileTiming ( ws2812_rmt :: Variant :: Ws2812bV5 ), 20'000'000 , 0 ); const size_t longest = ws2812_rmt :: MaxPixelsAtRate ( 30 , 3 , wave . value ); // 1058 const uint64_t frame_ns = ws2812_rmt :: FrameTimeNs ( 60 , 3 , wave . value ); // 2 172 000 ns const uint32_t level_mv = ws2812_rmt :: MinLogicHighMv ( ws2812_rmt :: Variant :: Ws2812bV5 , 5000 ); // 2750 static_cast < void > ( longest ); static_cast < void > ( frame_ns ); static_cast < void > ( level_mv ); } A 60-pixel WS2812B strip takes about 2.2 ms per frame, and a 1024-pixel strip about 32 ms (the datasheets promise at least 1024 pixels at 30 frames per second). A frame is sent in one gapless stream and the call blocks until it and the reset are out; the reference ESP32 port runs the stream without the CPU (RMT, with DMA where the part has it) and then spends the reset (300 µs) in a busy wait of the CPU. The port must not underrun: see Porting . Mixed chains ¶ Pixels of two WS2812B generations in one chain need one waveform inside both windows, and for the 2013 and V5 generations there is none. WaveformInWindow() tells which variants accept a waveform: timing.cpp // Two generations in one chain: is one waveform legal for both? bool OneWaveformServesBoth () { const auto wave = ws2812_rmt :: ResolveWaveform ( ws2812_rmt :: ProfileTiming ( ws2812_rmt :: Variant :: Ws2812bV5 ), 20'000'000 , 0 ); return wave && ws2812_rmt :: WaveformInWindow ( ws2812_rmt :: Variant :: Ws2812bV5 , wave . value ) && ws2812_rmt :: WaveformInWindow ( ws2812_rmt :: Variant :: Ws2812bPreV5 , wave . value ); // false: use Custom } When it returns false for a pair you must have, measure which waveform both strips accept and declare it with Custom ( Configuration ), or split the strip into two outputs. What is not covered ¶ WS2812E is not named: no datasheet could be obtained for it. Reach it through Custom once you hold its sheet. WS2812D-F5 is the same family as the F8 and unverified; the current WS2812B V7 sheet was not obtained. The original WS2812 lists a low-speed 400 kbit/s mode with no windows. It is reachable through Custom . WS2811 and other drivers with a 400 kbit/s mode, dual-signal parts (a backup data line), SPI-clocked pixels and 16-bit-per-channel parts use a different frame or wire. No datasheet gives the pixel's power-on reset time or an upper bound for the reset: both are assumptions with a knob ( Limitations ).

WS2811 and other drivers with a 400 kbit/s mode, dual-signal parts (a backup data line), SPI-clocked pixels and 16-bit-per-channel parts use a different frame or wire. No datasheet gives the pixel's power-on reset time or an upper bound for the reset: both are assumptions with a knob ( Limitations ).
